topics: Excel Basics & Core Functions: Interface, data types, formulas
Lookup functions, conditional functions, and text functions.

Charts & Visualization Methods: Bar, line, pie, scatter, combo charts, advanced charting, conditional formatting for insights.
Interactive Dashboards: PivotCharts, KPI visuals, storytelling layouts, mini dashboard creation.
Data Modeling & Power Tools: Power Pivot, relationships, basic DAX concepts, Excel add-ins for extended analytics.

projects: A/B Test Readout for a pricing experiment

modules.name: SQL (Structured Query Language)
topics: Core SQL & RDBMS Basics: Syntax, data types, tables, CRUD operations, querying single tables.
Filtering & Retrieval: WHERE, ORDER BY, DISTINCT, logical operators, formatting results.
Joins & Multi-Table Queries: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, CROSS joins, UNION, subqueries, nested queries.
Aggregations & Analytics: GROUP BY, HAVING, summary stats, ranking functions, Top-N analysis.
Views & Modifications: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, creating views, inline views.
Optimization: Indexes, execution plans, performance tuning.
Advanced Database Concepts: Normalization, stored procedures, functions, triggers, user-defined objects.
SQL in Practice: Integrating SQL with Python, advanced analytical queries for real datasets.

modules.name: PowerBI
topics: Data Prep with Power Query: Clean, transform,merge, unpivot, format text/date/number fields.
Data Modeling: Relationships, granularity, aggregations, time-series basics, calculated columns.
Core Visuals & Interactivity: Bar, pie, line, maps, cards, slicers, filters, drill-down, bookmarks.
Connecting & Working with Data: Load from Excel/SQL, model views, query editor, BI best practices.
Advanced Visuals: Funnel, ribbon, waterfall, treemap, gauge, scatter, KPIs & combos.
DAX for Analytics: Measures, calculations, time intelligence functions.
Dashboard Design: Layouts, formatting, interactivity, storytelling, sharing & collaboration.
Projects: Customer segmentation dashboard, exploratory BI reports, hands-on visual assignments.

modules.name: Tableau
topics: Connecting & Preparing Data: Data types, joins, blending, pivots, transformations, SQL connections.
Core Visual Building: Bar, line, pie, scatter, bubble, maps (geo, custom geocoding, polygon, WMS).
Data Exploration Tools: Filters, groups, sets, parameters, drill-down, marks, dimensions & measures.
View & Layout Tools: Shelves, cards, sorting, formatting, captions, exporting, metadata management.
Advanced Visuals: Funnel, ribbon, waterfall, treemap, gauge, scatter, KPIs & combos.
Advanced Visuals: Tree maps, heat maps, bump charts, funnel, waterfall, histogram, bullet & motion charts.
Calculations & Analytics: Calculated fields, LOD expressions, trends, forecasting, predictive visuals.
Dashboards & Storytelling: Interactive dashboards, stories, actions, design best practices, publishing & collaboration (Tableau Online).
Projects & Applications: Build multi-chart dashboards, map-based visuals, predictive model integration.

personas.name: College student (not yet graduated)
personas.signals: Pursuing any degree; 1st–3rd year; preparing for placements
pains: Wants something on the resume beyond the degree
Doesn't know which career to pick
personas.why: Short, no-code and useful in any role, so it doesn't lock a student into one career.
probes: Which degree and year are you in?
Do you want to code, or use AI tools?
personas.note: Only DABA's graduate requirement is defined. Confirm whether IIT Patna certificates need graduation before promising them.

personas.name: Non-graduate (12th or diploma)
personas.signals: Not studying; 12th pass or diploma; may be working or self-employed
pains: Many job openings require a degree
personas.why: Fits if they are working, freelancing or running a business and will use AI directly.
probes: Are you working, freelancing or running a business?
Are you planning to finish a degree?
What do you want AI to do for you?
personas.note: Don't promise placement outcomes. If their goal is a salaried job, hand them to a counsellor.

personas.name: Fresher with a CS/IT/engineering degree
personas.signals: 0–1 year; B.Tech/BCA/MCA/B.Sc CS; can code a little
personas.why: The broadest entry path into data and AI, with a project portfolio and capstones.
probes: What have you built in code?
Do you prefer data and numbers, or building apps?
personas.note: Engineering programs (SDE, FDE, GenAI for Developers) need 1+ year of experience. Offer them after the first job.

personas.name: Fresher with a non-CS degree
personas.signals: B.Com, BBA, BA, B.Sc (non-CS), MBA fresher
pains: Wants a corporate job beyond sales or BPO
personas.why: Starts with Excel, statistics, SQL and BI, the skills analyst jobs screen for.
probes: How comfortable are you with Excel?
Which roles are you applying for?
Would you try a little Python?

personas.name: Career-gap returnee
personas.signals: 6 months+ gap: maternity, health, exams, layoff
personas.why: Non-tech returnees → DABA; tech returnees → Data Science & GenAI Program. Both give fresh projects that explain the gap.
probes: What was your role before the break?

personas.name: Marketing, design or content professional
personas.signals: Marketer, graphic/UI designer, content writer, social media manager, video editor
pains: Hours lost on resizes and variants
personas.why: Marketing & Creative track: AI images, video, voice, ad variants, SEO and AI-search content, campaign automation.
probes: Which tools do you use daily (Canva, Adobe, Figma)?
Do you want to grow in this role or switch?
personas.note: Upsell to DABA (Marketing analytics track) if they want a marketing-analyst job. Offer the AI Leadership Program to creative heads who manage teams.

personas.name: Non-tech professional staying in role
personas.signals: Sales, HR, finance, operations, consulting, teaching
personas.why: No-code AI with a function track for sales, HR or finance and operations.
probes: Which tasks take most of your week?
Which AI tools have you tried?

personas.name: Non-tech professional switching to analytics
personas.signals: 2–10 years in sales, ops, BPO, banking ops, HR or marketing; wants an analyst title
personas.why: Turns domain experience into an analyst profile; a domain track keeps them in their own industry.
probes: Which domain have you worked in?
What salary jump are you targeting?

personas.name: Working analyst moving into data science
personas.signals: MIS, BI, reporting, business or data analyst; knows Excel/SQL/Power BI
pains: Hit the ceiling of dashboard work
No ML or Python on resume
personas.why: Builds on SQL and BI and adds Python, statistics, ML and GenAI.
probes: How much Python have you written?

personas.name: Data scientist, data engineer or ML engineer
personas.signals: Writes Python daily; builds models or pipelines; wants GenAI and agent skills
pains: No production LLM work to show
personas.why: The Data & Analytics elective (text-to-SQL, data agents, conversational BI) with advanced RAG and LLMOps.
probes: Have you shipped an LLM feature?
Want CV and MLOps depth instead?

personas.name: Developer (1–5 years) moving into AI
personas.signals: Service-company developer; Java/.NET/Python/JS
personas.why: Five months, developer-only: LLM apps, RAG, agents, evals and AI system design.
probes: Which stack do you work on?

personas.name: Developer targeting a product company
personas.signals: 1–6 years; FAANG or product-company goal; fails DSA or system-design rounds
pains: Rejected in DSA or system-design rounds
personas.why: DSA (in Java, C++ or Python) and LLD/HLD come first, then GenAI.

personas.name: Senior developer, backend, full-stack or solutions engineer
personas.signals: 4–12 years; builds APIs and services; open to client-facing work
pains: Wants an AI title, not just AI on the resume
Needs enterprise RAG and agent experience
personas.why: Software engineering, advanced RAG, LLMOps, AI system design and client solutioning in one path.
probes: Do you enjoy client and stakeholder work?
Which cloud do you deploy on?

personas.name: QA or test engineer
personas.signals: Manual or automation tester; Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, Pytest
pains: Wants DevOps or AI testing skills
personas.why: If the goal is DevOps: Cloud & DevOps role track with the QA & Test specialisation.
probes: Interested in CI/CD and cloud, or in AI-driven testing?
personas.note: If the goal is AI testing, offer the GenAI & Agentic AI Master (AI-driven testing).

personas.name: Cloud, DevOps, SRE or platform engineer
personas.signals: Already works on AWS/Azure, CI/CD, Kubernetes
pains: Asked to run LLM workloads without training
Wants an AI platform or LLMOps role
personas.why: Agents, LLMOps and AI infrastructure for people who already know cloud.
probes: Run AI platforms or build AI apps?

personas.name: IT infrastructure professional moving to cloud
personas.signals: IT support/ITOps, system admin, network engineer, DBA; 1+ year
personas.why: One program; pick the role track that matches their job.

personas.name: Non-IT person asking about cloud jobs
personas.signals: No IT background; heard cloud pays well
personas.why: Cloud programs need 1+ year of IT experience. Analytics is the realistic tech entry for non-IT people.
probes: Have you used a command line or written a script?
personas.note: Be upfront that cloud programs require IT experience. Don't sell CD to this lead.

personas.name: Tech manager, engineering lead or architect
personas.signals: 2+ years; delivery manager, EM, architect, or an MBA in a manager role
pains: Team is ahead of them on AI
personas.why: Strategy, ROI, governance and AI delivery management, no coding.
probes: Which AI initiative is on your table?
personas.note: If they still code and want to build, offer the GenAI & Agentic AI Master.

personas.name: Business leader, founder or CXO
personas.signals: Business head, founder, consultant; wants AI strategy
pains: Pressure to have an AI strategy
personas.why: No-code leadership program with a capstone on their own organisation's AI plan.
probes: What business outcome do you want?
Build yourself or lead a team?

personas.name: Domain professional in BFSI, healthcare, manufacturing or retail
personas.signals: Analyst, risk, ops, product or engineering person in their industry (e.g. robotics, automation, process engineering); coding is taught from scratch
pains: Wants AI roles inside their industry
personas.why: Two domain specialisations on top of the GenAI core.
personas.note: If they don't code, route them to DABA (domain analytics track) or AAP.

personas.name: Tech professional who 'wants AI' with no target role
personas.signals: Any IT role; vague goal; comparing institutes
personas.why: Broadest master; specialisations are chosen in month 6, after the core.
probes: What do you want to be doing in 12 months?

personas.name: Lead who needs a formal degree
personas.signals: Mentions MS, M.Tech, degree, immigration, HR policy
pains: Needs a degree for promotion, visa or policy
personas.why: Only degree route. Needs a bachelor's with 60%+.
probes: Do you need a degree, or will a certification work?
Is it for promotion, visa or a job requirement?

routing.question: Did a tech professional ask about FDE (Forward Deployed AI Engineer)?
routing.rule: Yes → recommend Forward Deployed AI Engineer first, before the default mapping. Only redirect if they don't code at all; for newer coders, add Python and backend pre-work.

routing.question: Does the lead code at work, or have a CS/IT degree?
routing.rule: No → AAP, DABA or AIL. Yes → continue.

routing.question: How much work experience?
routing.rule: 0 years → fresher programs only (AAP, DABA, DS & GenAI Program). 1+ year → any program. AI Leadership needs 2+ years, including MBAs in manager roles; no 8-year minimum.

routing.question: Are they a graduate?
routing.rule: No → AAP only (confirm IIT Patna eligibility). Students still studying → AAP now, DABA or DSG-C after graduating.

routing.question: Current role
routing.rule: Developer, data, cloud/infra, QA, manager, domain specialist or fresher → see lead types.

routing.question: Goal
routing.rule: Use AI in current role · switch role · product-company jump · lead AI adoption · formal degree.

projects.outcome: A GPU-autoscaled inference platform with per-team cost tracking.

projects.title: QA Intelligence Platform
projects.objective: Generate tests, triage bugs and pick the right regression suite automatically.
projects.outcome: A QA assistant that writes tests from requirements and cuts regression run time.

projects.title: Food Image Tagging
projects.objective: Tag dishes and attributes automatically from menu photos.
projects.outcome: An image tagger that fills menu attributes and flags poor photos.

projects.title: Delivery Operations Dashboard
projects.objective: Give ops teams a live view of delays and AI explanations for each.
projects.outcome: A real-time dashboard with delay hotspots and auto-written incident notes.

projects.title: AI Transformation Plan for Your Organisation
projects.objective: Decide where AI will create value in your business and how to roll it out safely.
projects.outcome: A board-ready plan with prioritised use cases, ROI, governance and a 90-day pilot.

projects.title: AI Vendor Evaluation Scorecard
projects.objective: Choose between AI vendors on evidence, not demos.
projects.outcome: A scored comparison of 3 vendors on accuracy, cost, security and fit.
